questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted an English-speaking location, and I heard great things about Australia in general before applying.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university does give a lot of information and they are easy to communicate with leading up to arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I booked a tour of the school and the law faculty, which I highly recommend, as it is a big school and you can get classes in different buildings. It is possible to book many different orientation events, and some of them were online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It depends on how and where you wish to find housing. I used
realestate.com.au
to find a studio, but be aware that most places require that you view the place in person before you send an application. I would also recommend viewing the places in person rather than through FaceTime or not viewing it at all, because my first studio turned out to be unclean and had a pest problem upon arrival, so I terminated the lease.
It is more common (and cheaper) to sublet a room in a shared space, which is easiest through flatmates or Facebook pages (search for the area name and "local loop" or "accommodations") and be mindful of scams. A lot of people move to and away from Sydney all the time and many people sublet their rooms furnished when they travel or are away, so there is a lot of activity in those groups.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommend living off campus and closer to the beach because other areas are better to live in, in my opinion. I would recommend Coogee or Bondi.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did apply for it, but didn't get an offer. I heard mixed reviews from others.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I went on my first semester of my master's, and the registration process happened in spring before I had actually passed all my courses for my bachelor's, which caused some complications in my process, but it all turned out fine.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process is a bit long and you have to gather a lot of different documents.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can contact the coordinator at your own university for help or the host university - I did both during the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration system was a bit complicated and confusing because exchange students are only approved for 4 classes by default, and then you have to make a request to be approved for any other classes in their catalogue. I applied for six other classes and was approved for all of them, but by the time I was approved, some of them had already filled up. I did get the classes I wanted in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Submit the E-Requests early, maybe even before course registration is opened if possible, and add any relevant classes you have passed as reasoning (such as classes passed in English or within similar fields).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some of them said "unrestricted", as it was electives, but I believe all students were post-graduate level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different from class to class. Some had problem questions which the seminar revolved around, and some were closer to a lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sports Law
Media Law
Intellectual Property: copyright and design
Evidence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Media Law, Sports Law and IP. They were all pretty interesting and easy to follow. Evidence was also interesting, but the teacher I had and the subject coordinator were not the best, and the course demanded more than others to pass.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The student visa was 7000 dkk but it is even more expensive now i believe.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Take away food is not that expensive and coffee is cheap. Rent is expensive, but it is a city of high demand, so it was expected, and I did pay more to live in a studio.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many, and you get introduced at O'day during orientation.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't join any clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definatly take some trips to other cities on the east coast. In sydney definatly try many different beaches and explore different areas. Do the coastal walks! Go to the weekly markets and find weekly events on tiktok or instagram.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to be social during the first classes or join Facebook groups to find other locals or students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They are used to more animals and insects due to the more tropical weather.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are so nice! They spend a lot of time at the beach or being active, such as on coastal walks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Time goes by very fast, so make a list of everything you want to see and start exploring. Be aware of the safety instructions on beaches in general. Pack clothes for weather changes because it can change from day to day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find Studocu notes for your courses to review before exams, get an Opal card for transportation and the Opal card app, Go to Kmart for anything you might need, and remember an adapter.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the different places you get to visit and the people you meet.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing, visa application and all the practical stuff leading up to it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
